title: Chance, turned into numbers
question: How do mathematicians turn a chancy outcome into something they can measure?
hook: Pick someone at random, and their height becomes a number that depends on the draw.
idea: A random variable is a function that assigns a value to each possible outcome, and its distribution says how likely the values are.

beats.prompt: A random variable is absolutely continuous. What is the chance it takes one exact value, taken as a single point?

choices.label: Zero, since probabilities go to intervals
A small positive amount that shrinks with more values
choices.feedback: It is tempting to spread chance over points, but for an absolutely continuous variable each single point must have probability zero.

choices.label: One divided by the number of possible values
choices.feedback: A continuous variable has uncountably many values, so there is no count to divide by. Probability is assigned to intervals instead.

beats.explain: An absolutely continuous variable has a density that assigns probabilities to intervals, and each individual point must have probability zero.

beats.prompt: Sort each description into the kind of random variable it fits.
items: Has a finite set of values
Described by a probability mass function
beats.explain: A finite or countably infinite range makes a variable discrete. An uncountably infinite range, usually an interval, makes it continuous.

beats.prompt: Match each term to what it means.
pairs: A particular outcome of a random variable
Chance of being at or below a value
Assigns a probability to each value of a discrete variable
beats.explain: These terms describe outcomes and distributions of random variables, with mass functions for discrete variables and densities for absolutely continuous ones.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which one?
steps: An absolutely continuous variable can land anywhere in an interval.
Its distribution is described by a density that assigns probabilities to intervals.
So a single exact value must have a solid chance, like one divided by the number of values.
So we ask about the chance of landing in an interval instead.
beats.explain: Each individual point has probability zero for an absolutely continuous variable. That is why probabilities are assigned to intervals.
